intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Stickler syndrome type VI (STL6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene (120270) on chromosome 20q13.

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type VI (STL6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the second case of autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygosity for a loss of function mutation in COL9A3, which encodes the α3 chain of type IX procollagen.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous COL9A3 mutation causing AR Stickler syndrome. The 'type VI' label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The COL9A3 gene is located on chromosome 20q13.
checks.evidence_quote: Type IX collagen is a heterotrimeric molecule formed by three genetically distinct chains: α1, α2, and α3 encoded by the COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 genes.
checks.explanation: The paper discusses the COL9A3 gene. The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added by the draft.

paragraphs.text: Stickler syndrome type VI is an autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder. Its main features are eye involvement, especially high myopia, and sensorineural hearing loss, sometimes with skeletal findings. It is one of the recessive forms of Stickler syndrome caused by defects in type IX collagen.

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type VI is an autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Stickler syndrome is a connective tissue disorder characterized by hearing loss, ocular anomalies, palatal defects, and skeletal abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The paper calls it a connective tissue disorder, and the COL9A3 form is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: A main feature of Stickler syndrome type VI is eye involvement, especially high myopia.
checks.evidence_quote: All of the Stickler syndrome patients with type IX collagen defects have exhibited high myopia, midface hypoplasia, and mild–severe hearing loss.
checks.explanation: High myopia is reported as a consistent feature.

checks.claim: A main feature of Stickler syndrome type VI is sensorineural hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: including moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss, high myopia, and both tibial and femoral bowing at birth.
checks.explanation: Sensorineural hearing loss is a main feature.

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type VI sometimes includes skeletal findings.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiographs demonstrated abnormal capital femoral epiphyses and mild irregularities of the vertebral endplates.

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type VI is one of the recessive forms of Stickler syndrome caused by defects in type IX collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: recessive forms have been associated with mutations of COL9A1 (OMIM 120210) and COL9A2 (OMIM 120260) genes. Type IX collagen is a heterotrimeric molecule formed by three genetically distinct chains: α1, α2, and α3 encoded by the COL9A1, COL9A2, and COL9A3 genes.
checks.explanation: It follows directly that the recessive COL9A3 form is another recessive Stickler form caused by defects in type IX collagen.

paragraphs.text: Faletra et al. (2014) reported a consanguineous family in which affected members had features consistent with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, including high myopia and sensorineural hearing loss.

checks.claim: Faletra et al. (2014) reported a consanguineous family whose affected members had features consistent with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we describe the first autosomal recessive Stickler family
checks.explanation: The abstract describes an autosomal recessive Stickler family. It does not say the family is consanguineous; that may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family reported by Faletra et al. (2014) had high myopia.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no clinical findings for the family. High myopia is not mentioned.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family reported by Faletra et al. (2014) had sensorineural hearing loss.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no clinical findings for the family. Sensorineural hearing loss is not mentioned.

paragraphs.text: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) described sibs with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome who had myopia and hearing loss.

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) described sibs with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: There is no report of hearing loss, myopia, other ocular anomalies, or skeletal anomalies in either parent or in the sister.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a single affected proband. His only sibling, a sister, is unaffected and heterozygous. The three affected siblings mentioned in the paper are Faletra et al.'s family, not a family Hanson-Kahn et al. reported.

checks.claim: The sibs with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome described by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) had myopia.
checks.evidence_quote: by 2 years, he had developed myopia of −6.75 OD and −8 OS. By 12 years, this had progressed to −10.75 OD and −11.25 OS.
checks.explanation: Myopia is reported, but in a single patient, not in sibs.

checks.claim: The sibs with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome described by Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) had hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Audiology evaluation at 5 months identified moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss on the right from 250 through 4,000 Hz and severe sensorineural hearing loss on the left
checks.explanation: Hearing loss is reported, but in a single patient, not in sibs.

paragraphs.text: The families reported by Faletra et al. (2014) and Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) showed that Stickler syndrome type VI is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

checks.claim: The families reported by Faletra et al. (2014) and Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) showed that Stickler syndrome type VI is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: In consanguineous Stickler syndrome family R08–308, exome sequencing was used to identify homozygosity for single base duplication c.650dupC in exon 13 of COL9A3
checks.explanation: The affected proband is homozygous, and the parents and an unaffected sibling are heterozygous, which fits AR inheritance. The paper also discusses the earlier COL9A3 family as AR.

paragraphs.text: Other autosomal recessive forms of Stickler syndrome are caused by mutations in the COL9A1 gene (Stickler syndrome type IV) and the COL9A2 gene (Stickler syndrome type V).

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type IV is an autosomal recessive form of Stickler syndrome caused by mutations in the COL9A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Five families have been described with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygosity for loss-of-function mutations in the COL9A1 and COL9A2 type IX procollagen genes
checks.explanation: AR forms due to COL9A1 are described. The type number is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: Stickler syndrome type V is an autosomal recessive form of Stickler syndrome caused by mutations in the COL9A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Five families have been described with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome due to homozygosity for loss-of-function mutations in the COL9A1 and COL9A2 type IX procollagen genes
checks.explanation: AR forms due to COL9A2 are described. The type number is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, Faletra et al. (2014) found a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the COL9A3 gene.

checks.claim: Faletra et al. (2014) found a homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene in affected members of a consanguineous family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: we describe the first autosomal recessive Stickler family due to loss of function mutations (c.1176_1198del, p.Gln393Cysfs*25) of COL9A3 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a COL9A3 mutation in an autosomal recessive Stickler family. It does not state that the mutation is homozygous or that the family is consanguineous. Only the abstract was available.

checks.claim: The homozygous COL9A3 mutation found by Faletra et al. (2014) in a consanguineous family with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome is a loss-of-function mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: due to loss of function mutations (c.1176_1198del, p.Gln393Cysfs*25) of COL9A3 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract explicitly calls the mutation loss-of-function.

paragraphs.text: In affected sibs with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome, Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) found a homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene.

checks.claim: Hanson-Kahn et al. (2018) found a homozygous mutation in the COL9A3 gene in affected sibs with autosomal recessive Stickler syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Genotyping of the parents and an unaffected sibling showed that all of them were heterozygous for the sequence change
checks.explanation: The homozygous COL9A3 c.650dupC mutation was found in a single proband, not in affected sibs. The only sibling is unaffected and heterozygous.
